newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks shun Dow rally again on Q1 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks shun Dow rally again on Q1 earnings.

text.p: Mexican stocks pared most earlier losses on month-end buying to close off a sliver on Wednesday, but failed for the second day in a row to match a rally on Wall Street amid market disappointment over first quarter earnings, analysts and traders said.

"Earnings that came in below expectations are still hurting the market, and economic growth still looks weak. That's why people do not much feel like buying," said Rodolfo Campuzano, an analyst at the Invex brokerage.
The leading IPC share index .MXX ended off 0.65 point, or 0.02 percent, at 3,756.61.
"Although the Dow reacted well today, the conditions for foreign investors to enter Mexico are now clear: wait for the results of (mid-term) elections and second quarter earnings," Campuzano added.
The Dow Jones meanwhile climbed 46.96 points to 7,008.99.
Lackluster trading volume .TV.MX of 78.9 million shares reflected a lack of investor interest, traders said.
Dealers said month-end buying in the closing minutes failed to turn blue chips around.
"Many buyers stepped in at the close, but there were too many orders to sell," a floor trader said.
"Sellers were anticipating the usual month-end rush, so those who tried to rescue prices couldn't turn the market around."
Telmex, which accounted for 21 percent of all shares traded, weighed most heavily on the upside, ending four centavos ahead at 16.46 pesos.
Conglomerate Grupo Carso, a market heavyweight, ended down 1.05 pesos at 45.90 pesos in the wake of slow earnings, traders said.
Traders said Kimberly Clark de Mexico (Kimber) was another blue chip that fell in response to poor earnings.
"The market has hit Kimber hard, because of its (earnings) report," a desk trader said. "Retail and soft drinks firms look better, because they are things people will not stop consuming."
Paper products maker Kimber, in which Kimberly Clark Corp has a minority stake, fell 45 centavos to 29.50 pesos.
Retail chain Cifra meanwhile gained eight centavos to 12.20 pesos.
On the broad market, 118 stocks were traded in total, of which gainers outnumbered sliders by 52 to 45.
Bus and truck maker Dina topped the prominent gainers' list .PG.MX, up 50 centavos to 5.80 pesos.
"Dina gained because its report was more or less in line with expectations, and they went after it considering how bad reports were on average," a desk trader said.
